SQL 156 adds two SECURITY DEFINER read functions and replaces nothing (owner 2026-11-11: "if a tenant uploads a check and shares the check with a partner, both the tenant and that partner's documents that are automatically shared with the mortgage team show up for the mortgage team", "It should be everybody shared on that check"): aws_mortgage_desk_shared_library_documents(uuid) lists the auto_share_mortgage_ops library:mortgage:% tenant_documents of every tenant on a Desk request's check (its own tenant, then the source and target of every unrevoked shared_checks row), and aws_mortgage_agent_can_read_shared_library_path(text[], text, uuid) is the matching check for opening one; both answer the platform owner or a mortgage agent while the request is open or assigned to them, EXECUTE checksops and the owner only. The spec prerequisites are the file's own (55000 sql156_prerequisite_missing); the applying login must reach mortgage_handling_requests, shared_checks, tenant_documents and tenants as the definer past RLS (definer_can_write_relations; the file refuses otherwise, sql156_definer_cannot_read). No table, column, policy, table grant, trigger or row changes, so the db-readonly-validate trigger count is not affected. Expected pre-state in both environments: both functions absent (release sql156 v1: 44259316206f9f591ce8f3a6d63b8627add30153669f612acf539e3eec6cda12, releaseStateHash('sql156', {})). The API (a Desk list action and the storage signer consulting the new path check) and the Desk page ship after this through their own guarded paths; no API, Lambda or SPA change is part of this pin.
